rulings_in_ledger_order: use a separate retrospective offline archive operation instead of relaxing current-day live validators or reacquiring completed sources — safely uses existing full immutable evidence and its original report clock — cost if wrong is that dashboard integration and automated archive delivery remain later work.

keep holdout, calibration, adoption and physical timing unverified regardless of aggregate size or score improvement — sample/day counts alone do not establish a prospective protocol or independent event clock — cost if wrong is delayed adoption until additional evidence is supplied.

require identical ordered three-phase model IDs/versions/parameters across the common cohort instead of pooling unlike configurations — avoids mixing versions or feature definitions in an average — cost if wrong is that legitimate cross-version research needs separate cohort calls.

persist an integrity index and computed report without an execution-COMPLETED marker — a delayed/failed final close must not turn a partial operation into a success claim — cost if wrong is that invocation success needs the CLI result and full restore verification rather than one standalone marker file.

when Windows cannot create a real symlink, execute equivalent fail-closed and preservation assertions using injected OS-link metadata instead of skipping or passing an empty test — keeps executable security coverage without new privileges — cost if wrong is that actual Windows link creation remains unexercised in that environment and must not be claimed.
